proof_method_executed: A directed single-DUT simulation of src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv driving real AHB-Lite writes and reads (8 expectations, of which exactly the two encoding the in-tree stickiness requirement fail, 2 witnesses observed, 2 coverage counters hit), plus a 5-gate structural audit over the submitted tree: the declared reset signals of the lock field and of the entry data field, the signal connected to the pv module's core_only_rst_b port and whether it is an internal signal or a top-level pin, the firmware reachability of that signal through the boot FSM and the register that drives it, what the lock protects, and the in-tree statements on PCR lock stickiness. Gates evaluated: 5 of 5. The gate that decides whether the finding is an attacker capability rather than a reset-domain curiosity is gate 3, returning pcr_lock_reset_reachable_from_firmware=1. The gate that decides whether there is a requirement to violate is gate 5, returning spec_pcr_lock_stickiness_statements=1 with spec_pcr_control_reset_column_rows=0, so the tree carries exactly one normative statement on the point and no contradicting one.
result_summary:
A set PCR lock bit is cleared by a microcontroller-only reset, which src/pcrvault/config/pcrvault.md:6 forbids: 'A lock bit can be set by FW to prevent the entry from being cleared. The lock bit is sticky and only resets on a powergood cycle.' The measurement the lock was protecting survives the same reset, and the clear that the lock refused before the reset is accepted after it and zeroes the measurement.

The root cause is a reset-domain mismatch between a protection bit and the asset it protects. src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:29-30 declares the lock field as sw=rw; swwel=true; hw=r with resetsignal = core_only_rst_b, while src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:22 declares the PCR entry data with resetsignal = hard_reset_b. The generated register block implements what the description declares: the lock storage element is clocked with negedge hwif_in.core_only_rst_b and resets to zero (generated_lock_flop_reset_by_core_only=1), so this is a property of real flops and not of an .rdl comment.

Reading resetsignal = core_only_rst_b is not on its own enough to call this a defect, because a reset domain that only an external pin can enter is not an attacker capability. Gate 2 therefore traces the module input rather than reading the port name: at the pv instantiation src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:1226 connects .core_only_rst_b (cptra_uc_rst_b), and cptra_uc_rst_b is not a top-level input pin (pv_reset_signal_is_top_level_input_pin=0). The pin-versus-internal detector is not trusted on that reading alone: the same extraction applied to the module's cptra_pwrgood port, which is the one condition the in-tree sentence does permit to clear the lock, correctly resolves to a top-level input pin (contrast_pwrgood_signal_is_top_level_input_pin=1). The distinction the case rests on is therefore a real one rather than an artefact of the extraction.

Gate 3 closes the reachability chain. cptra_uc_rst_b is the boot FSM output described in the tree as the 'Global + fw update rst that goes to VeeR core only' (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_boot_fsm.sv:37); the arc into the firmware-reset state is arc_BOOT_DONE_BOOT_FWRST = (boot_fsm_ps == BOOT_DONE) & fw_update_rst (:97); fw_update_rst is driven from a register field at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:334; and that field, internal_fw_update_reset.core_rst, is declared hw = r; sw = rw; singlepulse=true; swwel = soc_req at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_internal_reg.rdl:45. sw = rw makes it firmware-writable and swwel = soc_req excludes the SoC, so triggering this reset is specifically a firmware capability. The in-tree description agrees in prose: 'the firmware reset request is triggered by software' (src/integration/config/integration.md:1125).

What the lock protects, gate 4: src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:110-111 feeds the lock's own value into the swwel write-enable-low of both the lock field and the clear field, so the lock is the only gate on the clear, and src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:130 makes PCR_CTRL[entry].clear.value drive the entry data's hwclr. Losing the lock therefore hands software a path to zero a stored measurement.

Measured on the DUT, entry 7 with measurement 0x5ec00007. CONTROL_A: the provisioned entry reads back 0x5ec00007 over AHB, so the later readings are not vacuous. CONTROL_B: an AHB write sets PCR_CTRL[7].lock and it reads back set. CONTROL_C: with the lock set, an AHB write of the clear bit is refused (clear_bit=0) and the measurement survives at 0x5ec00007, so the protection is live and not merely declared. WITNESS_D: after a core_only_rst_b pulse with rst_b and cptra_pwrgood held asserted throughout, PCR_CTRL[7] reads 0x00000000 (lock=0) while the entry still reads 0x5ec00007. WITNESS_E: the same clear write that CONTROL_C proved was refused is now accepted and the entry reads 0x00000000. checks_run=8 checks_failed=2 witness_hits=2, with the two failures being exactly the two expectations that encode the in-tree stickiness requirement.

One alternative explanation was ruled out by measurement rather than by argument. The swwel terms at src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:110-111 are also masked by ~fw_update_rst_window, so a clear write lands while that window is asserted too — and there the mask is doing its documented job of keeping combinational paths out of other reset domains (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_boot_fsm.sv:89-91), not exhibiting a lock failure. fw_update_rst_window is a combinational function of the boot FSM state (swwel_mask_is_a_function_of_boot_fsm_state=2), so its scope is bounded to the reset edge, whereas the lock flop stays cleared indefinitely. WITNESS_E measures the window de-asserted at the moment the post-reset clear is issued, so the accepted clear is attributable to the lost lock and not to the mask.

impact: Loss of PCR measurement integrity. A PCR entry holds a boot measurement that an attestation quote is computed over. Firmware that can zero an entry and re-extend it controls what the platform attests to, which is the property PCR storage exists to provide.

The protection is defeated by an operation the design supports rather than by a fault. A firmware-update reset is a normal, documented firmware action; no glitching, no scan mode, no debug unlock, and no SoC cooperation is needed.

The window is not narrow. The lock flop stays cleared for as long as the design runs after the reset, until firmware sets it again, so an attacker is not racing a transient. Every PCR lock in the vault clears at once, since all 32 control registers share the reset domain.

The measurement itself survives, which is what makes the loss exploitable rather than self-limiting. Had the entry data cleared with its lock, there would be nothing left to protect and the plan pre-committed to withdrawing the claim; measured, the entry still read 0x5ec00007 after the reset.
security_impact_assessment.bypassed_feature: PCR lock stickiness across a firmware-update reset. src/pcrvault/config/pcrvault.md:6 states the lock bit is sticky and only resets on a powergood cycle; it is implemented with the microcontroller-only reset as its reset signal, which firmware itself can assert.
attacker_model: Caliptra runtime firmware executing at supervisor mode on the Caliptra microcontroller. It needs two capabilities, both of which the tree grants it: AHB access to the PCR vault control and entry registers, and the ability to write INTERNAL_FW_UPDATE_RESET.core_rst, whose swwel = soc_req excludes the SoC and leaves firmware as the permitted writer.

No physical access, no debug authorization, and no SoC-side action is required. The attack does not depend on any signal that only an external pin can drive, which is precisely what gate 2 was written to decide.

evidence.key_observation: Measured on one pv DUT over real AHB, entry 7 holding 0x5ec00007. Before the reset: PCR_CTRL[7]=0x00000001 (lock set), a clear write refused with clear_bit=0, entry still 0x5ec00007. After a core_only_rst_b pulse with rst_b and cptra_pwrgood held asserted: PCR_CTRL[7]=0x00000000 (witness_pcr_lock_survives_core_only_reset=0) while the entry still reads 0x5ec00007 (witness_pcr_measurement_survives_core_only_reset=1). The same clear write then lands and the entry reads 0x00000000 (witness_measurement_cleared_after_reset=1), with fw_update_rst_window measured de-asserted at that moment so the swwel mask does not explain it. checks_run=8 checks_failed=2 witness_hits=2, cover_locked_clear_refused=1, cover_unlocked_clear_landed=1. Audit: pcr_lock_resetsignal_is_core_only=1, pcr_data_resetsignal_is_hard_reset=1, lock_and_data_reset_domains_differ=1, generated_lock_flop_reset_by_core_only=1, pv_core_only_rst_connected_signal=cptra_uc_rst_b, pv_reset_signal_is_top_level_input_pin=0 against contrast_pwrgood_signal_is_top_level_input_pin=1, boot_fsm_fwrst_arc_uses_fw_update_rst=1, fw_update_rst_driven_by_register=1, fw_update_reset_field_software_writable=1, pcr_lock_reset_reachable_from_firmware=1, pv_lock_swwel_feedback_sites=2, pv_clear_to_data_hwclr_sites=1, swwel_mask_is_a_function_of_boot_fsm_state=2, spec_pcr_lock_stickiness_statements=1, spec_pcr_lock_stickiness_statements_in_hw_spec=1, spec_pcr_control_reset_column_rows=0. audit_conclusion=pcr_lock_reset_is_firmware_reachable_and_contradicts_the_in_tree_stickiness_requirement.
evidence.requirement_is_unambiguous: The tree carries exactly one normative statement on PCR lock stickiness, src/pcrvault/config/pcrvault.md:6, repeated once in the hardware specification (spec_pcr_lock_stickiness_statements_in_hw_spec=1), and no reset-column table row for the PCR control register that could name a different reset (spec_pcr_control_reset_column_rows=0). The requirement therefore has a single reading and the implementation contradicts it. This is the specific condition that makes the case decidable, and gate 5 measures it rather than asserting it.

non_findings: PRE-COMMITTED SCOPE LIMIT, held: this case does not claim that core_only_rst_b is the wrong reset signal for the KeyVault lock fields, even though those fields carry the same declaration (keyvault_lock_declarations_with_core_only_reset=3). The KeyVault has its own in-tree table rows naming a reset column for its lock fields (keyvault_lock_reset_column_rows_in_hw_spec=2), so the KeyVault declaration matches at least one of its own in-tree statements and the resulting ambiguity is a specification question rather than a defect this measurement can decide. The PCR vault has only the prose stickiness sentence and no such column, which is exactly why this case is decidable and the KeyVault equivalent is not. The contrast is recorded in the audit output and deliberately kept out of the verdict.

NOT MEASURED, recorded as the consequence this case does not itself demonstrate: that a cleared PCR entry can be usefully re-extended with attacker-chosen values to forge a quote. The PCR vault's single hardware write client is the SHA-512 hash-extend path, and whether a complete forging flow is reachable depends on the SHA-512 control sequence, which is outside a pv module-boundary measurement. The case claims the clear, which is already a loss of measurement integrity, and states re-extension as an unmeasured consequence rather than folding it into the verdict.

MEASURED WITHOUT A PRE-ASSIGNED VERDICT, as the plan required: whether PCR_CTRL.clear is a singlepulse field, and therefore whether the post-reset clear needs one write or a held value. It is declared singlepulse at src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:32, and one AHB write was sufficient — WITNESS_E issued a single write of the clear bit and the entry read back zero. This affects how the attack sequence is written but not whether it succeeds.

RULED OUT rather than assumed: the ~fw_update_rst_window qualifier on the swwel terms at src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:110-111 as an alternative explanation for the accepted clear. That mask makes a clear write land while the window is asserted, which would be an innocent reading of the same symptom, so it had to be separated from the lock loss. It is a combinational function of the boot FSM state (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_boot_fsm.sv:90-91), bounded to the reset edge and introduced to keep combinational paths out of other reset domains, whereas the lock flop stays cleared indefinitely. WITNESS_E asserts the window is de-asserted at the moment the post-reset clear is issued, so the two are separated by measurement.

NOT CLAIMED as part of this case: that the microcontroller-only reset clearing the lock is wrong for any other field in the PCR vault. The clear field at src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:32 declares no resetsignal override and the entry data at :22 uses hard_reset_b, so the lock field is the only one whose reset domain is being questioned here.
conclusion: Confirmed security bug. The PCR lock is declared with resetsignal = core_only_rst_b (src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:30), which at the pv instantiation is cptra_uc_rst_b (src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:1226), which the boot FSM asserts when firmware writes INTERNAL_FW_UPDATE_RESET.core_rst — a field declared sw = rw with the SoC excluded by swwel = soc_req. The protected measurement resets on hard_reset_b and survives that reset. Because the lock is the only gate on the clear (src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:110-111) and the clear drives the entry data's hardware clear (:130), firmware can set a lock, be refused a clear, trigger a firmware-update reset, and have the same clear land on a measurement that is still present. Measured end to end on one DUT: lock 1 to 0 across the reset with the entry intact at 0x5ec00007, then the previously refused clear zeroing it. This contradicts the tree's single statement on the point, src/pcrvault/config/pcrvault.md:6, that the lock bit is sticky and only resets on a powergood cycle, and no in-tree reset-column row for the PCR control register offers a competing reading. Two things are deliberately excluded from the verdict: the identically-declared KeyVault lock fields, which have their own in-tree reset column and are therefore ambiguous rather than decidable, and the re-extension step that would turn the clear into a forged quote, which a pv module-boundary measurement cannot reach.
